description: Read-only repository audit of versioned schemas, behavior contracts, policies and implementation identities. This file is not a runtime authorization registry and must not become one by accident.

scope.included: Persisted formats, boundary validators, runtime route/auth decisions, evidence expiry and migration branches.
scope.excluded: Ordinary UI labels, comments without a consumer, dependency/library semver and historical evidence that is not read by a current route unless referenced by a current validator.

classification_rules.Schema: Data shape and compatibility. It answers whether an old or new document can be decoded and migrated.
classification_rules.Contract: Stable externally observable behavior or security semantics.
classification_rules.Policy: A current threshold, gate or acceptance rule.
classification_rules.Identity: The concrete producer, executable, CLI, Core, toolchain, ruleset or content, preferably a digest.
classification_rules.MIXED / NEEDS_SPLIT: One identifier currently carries two or more of Schema, Contract, Policy and Identity responsibilities. Do not split it in this audit.

entries.risk: Low. The schema is a real persisted boundary, but migration ownership must stay at import.
entries.recommendation: Keep v1. Concentrate decode/validate/migrate/normalize at the project boundary; do not add a second business-layer version check.

entries.risk: Low to medium. A package is read-only, so confusing it with an active .ck project would damage recovery semantics.
entries.recommendation: Keep the schema axis separate from package identity and source-content SHA-256.

entries.risk: Medium. It remains a compatibility input and must not silently receive V2-only certification.
entries.recommendation: Read and migrate at the package boundary only. Do not create V3 to replace it.

entries.risk: High if V2 metadata and legacy V1 handling remain interleaved in catalog logic.
entries.recommendation: Preserve strict V2 and fail-closed behavior. Future changes should be compatible fields or a boundary migration, not V3 in this project.

entries.risk: Medium. Generator format and generated-code semantics can be confused with implementation identity.
entries.recommendation: Keep the data schema at v1; bind generator implementation/content by digest when evidence is produced.

entries.risk: Medium. Board identity, Core recommendation and certification status must not be treated as one version.
entries.recommendation: Keep package Schema v1; use board/content/Core/toolchain digests for evidence identity.

entries.risk: High. A persisted Schema contains a behavior-contract field, so a harmless producer change can look like a breaking board format change.
entries.recommendation: Retain ck.lock v1 for compatibility. Future work should separate `format_schema`, `certification_contract_id`, producer identity and evidence digests without changing V2 block behavior.

entries.risk: High when validator version, ruleset and contract hash are interpreted as Schema compatibility.
entries.recommendation: Keep report Schema v2. Treat validator/ruleset as policy and producer identity; revalidate old reports instead of inventing report v3.

entries.current_name: Package quality ruleset / validator / contract hash
entries.risk: High. A ruleset threshold or validator implementation change can be mistaken for a report-contract break.
entries.recommendation: Keep report Schema independent. Use `policy_id` for acceptance rules and SHA-256 for validator/ruleset content; old reports should become stale and be rechecked.

entries.risk: Low. This is a tool release identity, not a package Schema.
entries.recommendation: Keep semantic release versioning, but identify the executable and rules by digest when an artifact is used for certification.

entries.risk: Medium. Engine identity, build behavior and certificate format are currently presented together.
entries.recommendation: Freeze public behavior. Do not create a new Forge version for implementation-only changes; update producer identity and revalidate evidence.

entries.risk: High after fix. The former v8/v9 disagreement could reject valid evidence or make different binaries authorize different contracts; active layers are now aligned.
entries.recommendation: Use the Rust builder marker as the runtime authority. Reject historical v8 evidence and requalify it; do not alias v8 to v9 or create v10. Implementation/evidence identity changes invalidate evidence unless behavior is actually breaking.

entries.risk: High. The v13 name is an identity-key convention while the v6 number is a cache document format; they are separate axes with overlapping names.
entries.recommendation: Keep old readers fail-closed. Future identity should be a component digest set; cache serialization Schema can evolve independently at the boundary. Do not increment the identity name for ordinary scanner implementation changes.

entries.risk: High. The 20% ESP32 library policy and 25% general policy can produce incomparable green results.
entries.recommendation: Keep policy separate from build contract. Freeze FLFE policy while auditing; record workload scope explicitly. Do not silently promote a 20% specialized result to a target-wide 25% certificate.

entries.risk: Critical. Certificate structure, behavior contract, policy and producer identity all affect one authorization decision.
entries.recommendation: Do not add another certificate schema in this governance phase. Later separate envelope Schema, contract/policy references and producer/subject digests; old certificates must be revalidated, not re-labeled.

entries.risk: High. Adapter implementation identity is encoded as a behavior-contract name, and each adapter can create another independent axis.
entries.recommendation: Freeze current adapter contracts. Future adapter metadata should distinguish stable capability semantics from producer implementation digest; no new adapters or certificate schemas during FLFE freeze.

entries.risk: Medium to high. This is a qualification-only route, but its manifest, evidence semantics and policy are all independently versioned.
entries.recommendation: Keep as historical/qualification evidence. Do not wire it into general runtime without a boundary adapter and policy scope; changes should first update identity and rerun evidence.

entries.risk: High. Capability, access control, translation proof and manifest serialization are intertwined.
entries.recommendation: Freeze the existing phase-1 routes. Keep schema parsing at the module boundary; do not add a new Fast route or adapter as part of this governance work.

entries.risk: Medium. Internal optimization evidence can be mistaken for a public certificate.
entries.recommendation: Keep internal and fail-closed. Use core/toolchain/object digests for invalidation; do not promote this to a new public contract.

entries.risk: Medium. The module explicitly says observation is not authorization, but downstream policy must preserve that boundary.
entries.recommendation: Keep schema v2 as an internal observation format. Do not let it grant Fast or create another capability contract.

entries.risk: Medium. Artifact role policy is legitimate, but IDs are repeated in multiple consumers.
entries.recommendation: Keep policy IDs, add a single inventory owner and test for duplicate definitions. Do not turn each artifact-policy revision into a build contract.

entries.risk: High if a display report version becomes an authorization gate or if it duplicates Forge contract constants.
entries.recommendation: Keep display/report Schemas at their boundary. The UI should consume normalized diagnostics and display a separate contract/identity result; do not let UI schema versions decide Fast authorization.

entries.risk: Medium. Report schemas are valid, but verifier branches are distributed and may be mistaken for public authorization contracts.
entries.recommendation: Keep report formats local to the runner. Centralize decoding later; never use a report schema revision alone to grant Fast.

entries.current_name: Internal cache, recovery, checkpoint, upload and diagnostic formats
versions: mostly schemaVersion/schema_version=1; hotset=2; build meta=3; toolchain cache=6/7; upload manifest=1; recovery/checkpoint=1
entries.risk: Medium. These are legitimate local Schemas, but many independent names make global audits and migration coverage difficult.
entries.recommendation: Do not merge them in this audit. Register each public/persisted format, keep local cache schemas internal, and later centralize boundary adapters without a giant framework.

entries.current_name: Build signature, property contract SHA-256, source/toolchain/content identities
versions: implementation-defined; digest fields include buildSignature, propertyContractSha256, source/content SHA-256
entries.risk: Medium. A digest is appropriate, but names such as property_contract can imply a new behavior contract.
entries.recommendation: Prefer named digest scopes and producer IDs. A changed implementation or ruleset should expire evidence through identity, not automatically become Contract vN.

entries.risk: Low. It is a data-only migration format and must remain non-executable.
entries.recommendation: Keep v1 and reject executable or unknown migration shapes. Do not create a second migration contract for V2.

entries.risk: Low to medium. Channel data includes artifact identity and publication status; it should not become an extension behavior contract.
entries.recommendation: Keep schema v1. Treat artifact URL, bytes and SHA-256 as release Identity.

entries.risk: Low. It is an integrity envelope, not a generator or package behavior contract.
entries.recommendation: Keep the sidecar Schema and bind the concrete artifact by SHA-256; do not couple it to package quality report versions.

entries.risk: Medium after fix. The manifest is a static candidate boundary and must not be mistaken for Fast performance authorization.
entries.recommendation: Keep the manifest on schema v2 with the current builder v9 marker. It has no performance_ab rows and cannot grant Fast; historical v8 inputs remain reject-only.

entries.risk: High when the report/certificate format is used as a proxy for the policy or build contract.
entries.recommendation: Keep these as data formats. Policy IDs and producer/target digests carry semantics and expiry; do not introduce a combined v5 for implementation changes.

entries.risk: Medium. Artifact structure and artifact equivalence policy are separate but currently adjacent in the same qualification path.
entries.recommendation: Keep schema versions at v1 and policy IDs separate. A changed artifact identity should expire evidence, not change the build Contract.

entries.risk: Medium. Nested versions make the report look like a contract family even though it is evidence transport.
entries.recommendation: Keep the transport Schema; later normalize nested records at the report boundary.

entries.risk: Medium. The metadata shape is consumed but has no explicit format version, so changes can be mistaken for arbitrary content differences.
entries.recommendation: Do not add a version just for this audit. First document the currently accepted shape; add a backward-compatible optional field only when a real migration need exists.

entries.risk: Medium. The profile remains in code for compatibility and can be mistaken for the current universal Fast route.
entries.recommendation: Keep historical read/deny behavior only. Do not generate new PortableFast evidence or expand its adapter/policy surface.

findings.summary: F-001 resolved: stale Forge v8 contract and bundled candidate identity were aligned to the current builder v9 marker.
findings.impact: The former split could reject valid evidence or make a certificate produced by one layer unusable in another. Current active layers now share one authority; unproven or historical v8 evidence still fails closed.
findings.action: Completed 2026-08-25 as a minimal compatibility bugfix: builder marker is authoritative, bundled candidate manifest is aligned, and cross-layer/history rejection tests are present. No v8 alias, no v10, no gate relaxation.

findings.summary: Performance policy is duplicated with different thresholds and workload scopes.
findings.impact: A specialized 20% result can be confused with the general 25% qualification rule.
findings.action: Keep separate policy IDs and explicitly bind workload scope. Freeze FLFE policy until a later policy review.

findings.summary: Certificate and passport payloads mix Schema, behavior Contract, Policy and producer Identity.
findings.impact: Implementation-only changes require broad certificate version churn and make expiry rules hard to explain.
findings.action: Future split at the boundary; keep existing schemas and fail-closed checks unchanged in this phase.

findings.summary: Toolchain identity names combine a cache serialization revision with a portable identity-key convention.
findings.impact: A scanner or cache implementation change can be mistaken for a new compatibility contract.
findings.action: Retain v13 as a legacy identity input; later normalize to component digests and keep cache Schema versioning at the boundary.

findings.summary: Version branches leak into catalog, package and reporting services.
findings.impact: Business consumers each learn historical versions and can diverge on migration or authorization behavior.
findings.action: Phase 2 boundary adapters: decode, validate, migrate and normalize once, then make consumers use a canonical model.

findings.summary: Portable/local performance and NativeRelink certificates reuse the same schemaId with different schema versions and payload meanings.
findings.impact: Readers must inspect both schemaId and schemaVersion, increasing the chance that a future consumer accepts the wrong certificate family.
findings.action: Keep both current formats for compatibility; later give certificate families distinct stable schema IDs or a single envelope with an explicit kind. This is a boundary cleanup, not a new runtime framework.

non_goals: No V3 Block Package design or V2 rewrite.
No new FLFE board qualification, adapter, certificate schema or performance route.
No fail-closed relaxation and no removal of historical evidence.
